findings.finding: The AC 'a test asserts the DC client is constructed WITHOUT `verify=False`' uses the wrong parameter form for pycontribs/jira. A test that only checks for the absence of a `verify=False` kwarg would pass even when TLS verification is disabled through the options dict, making the fixture invalid and the criterion unproven.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an observability requirement: the transport MUST emit structured log entries (at least DEBUG for retries, WARNING for non-retried HTTP errors, ERROR for auth/config failures) so operators can diagnose DC connectivity issues; add an AC or test asserting a retry attempt produces a log record naming the URL and attempt count.
evidence: 'Retry, timeout, and error typing are mapped onto rebar's existing transport contract — transient connectivity faults retried with the same 2s/5s backoff as adapters/jira/acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry'
No AC or test requirement mentions logging, metrics, or tracing for transport failures or retry events
The ACs cover error-raise behavior and retry call counts but not operator-visible instrumentation
findings.finding: The plan specifies retry/backoff and error surfacing but does not mention any logging or instrumentation of transport-level events (retry attempts, auth failures, slow responses, Jira DC unavailability). Operators deploying the DC backend would have no visibility into connectivity issues, repeated retries, or degraded performance without structured log output from the transport layer.
findings.location: Approach (retry/backoff paragraph) and Testing section — no observability requirement stated
scenarios: Jira DC instance is intermittently slow; reconciler retries silently; operator has no log evidence to diagnose the issue
Auth token expires; transport raises; no structured log captures which host/project failed or why
On-call engineer investigates a failed reconciliation run and finds no transport-level log entries to correlate with Jira DC downtime
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section, add: 'Each retry attempt emits a `logger.debug("jira-dc retry %d/%d: %s", attempt, max_attempts, url)` entry; non-retried HTTP errors emit `logger.warning`; ConfigError and auth failures emit `logger.error`.' Add a corresponding AC: 'a retry attempt produces a structured log record at DEBUG level naming the endpoint and attempt number.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the idempotency posture for write operations: either (a) writes are NOT retried (retry applies only to reads/probes) and the plan should say so explicitly, or (b) writes use Jira's idempotency mechanisms (e.g., `External-Issue-ID` header or pre-flight existence check) and a test covers the duplicate-prevention path.
evidence: 'transient connectivity faults retried with the same 2s/5s backoff'
No mention of idempotency keys, deduplication, or 'check-then-write' guards for create/comment/link operations
The live test exercises the happy path but does not include a 'retry after partial write' scenario
findings.finding: The plan does not address idempotency of write operations (create ticket, add comment, add link, transition). If the Jira DC server processes a write but the HTTP response is lost (e.g., connection reset after a successful POST), the transport's retry logic will re-issue the request, potentially creating duplicate tickets or duplicate comments with no way to detect the duplication.
findings.location: Approach (retry/backoff paragraph); Testing (live test: create → read → update → transition → comment → link)
scenarios: create_ticket POST succeeds on Jira DC but response is dropped by a network proxy; retry creates a second ticket with the same fields
add_comment is retried after a timeout; the ticket accumulates duplicate comments
link creation is retried; Jira DC creates two duplicate links
findings.suggested_fix: The simplest safe posture: restrict retry logic to idempotent operations (GET, absence probe) and raise immediately on write failures without retry, matching typical REST client conventions. Add one sentence to the Approach: 'Write operations (create, comment, link, transition) are NOT retried; only read and probe operations retry on transient faults.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `jira.JIRA` client instantiation strategy in `transport.py` (per-transport-instance, per-call, or explicit singleton with a lock) and document whether concurrent transport calls are safe; if a single instance is shared, add a note on thread-safety or wrap access with a lock.
evidence: Plan says the library is 'imported lazily inside the functions that need it' but does not state whether a single JIRA client instance is reused across calls or re-created per call.
pycontribs/jira wraps requests.Session internally; requests.Session is not documented as thread-safe for concurrent requests.
No mention of locking, connection-pool sizing, or per-call instantiation strategy anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan does not specify whether the `jira.JIRA` client instance is created once per transport instance (shared across calls), per-call, or as a module-level singleton, and does not address concurrent-access safety. The pycontribs/jira library wraps a `requests.Session`, which is not safe for concurrent use from multiple threads without external locking. If rebar ever calls transport methods concurrently (e.g. parallel ticket reconciliation), a shared client instance is a latent data-race.
findings.location: Approach section / `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`
scenarios: rebar reconciles a sprint's tickets in parallel threads — two threads call transport methods simultaneously on a shared JIRA client, corrupting session state or producing interleaved responses.
A future refactor caches the client at module level for performance, silently introducing a race that the plan gave no guidance to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Instantiate the `jira.JIRA` client once per `JiraDatacenterTransport` object (i.e., stored as `self._client` at `__init__` time), document that each transport instance is intended for single-threaded use, and note in the class docstring that callers needing concurrency should create one transport instance per thread. Alternatively, if rebar's engine already serializes transport calls, add a comment citing that guarantee.

findings.finding: The plan's Scope omits `adapters/__init__.py`, which is an unenumerated consumer that must be updated to import the DC backend module so it self-registers with `_backend_registry`. Currently `adapters/__init__.py` line 15 explicitly imports `from .jira import backend as _jira_backend` (the side-effect that calls `register()`). Without a corresponding import of the new DC backend, `select_backend('jira-datacenter')` will raise a KeyError at runtime even though the package is installed.

findings.finding: The Scope names the live test file as `tests/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`, but J5 (c97f-90ae-4976-47c7, closed) established the DC harness at `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` with full tier enforcement.
